method: Re-ran both named probes from scratch (fresh subprocess pytest invocations, not a re-read of the artifact); attempted to falsify the headline order-dependent and flaky counts by (a) checking the shuffle control is real, (b) checking the ground-truth fixtures are correctly classified, (c) running probe1 and probe2 multiple additional times to see whether the reported candidate/flake counts are stable or an artifact of a single lucky run, and (d) confirming the two excluded collection-error trees genuinely fail to collect without --ignore (i.e. the 138-test scope is not silently hiding tests).
commands_run: python3 -m pytest command-center/ --collect-only -q -p no:cacheprovider (without ignores, to confirm the excluded trees genuinely fail collection)
confirmed: Shuffle control is real, not a fake green: across 6 independent probe1 runs, the three recorded post-shuffle seed orders were pairwise distinct and each differed from the declaration-order baseline every time (shuffle_control_ok=True on every run); same_test_membership held (no tests dropped or duplicated by the shuffle).

Ground-truth order-dependent pair (test_a_writes_flag / test_b_requires_writer_flag) was correctly classified on every one of the 6 probe1 runs: flagged=True, failed exactly on seeds [1001, 2002] (the two seeds whose shuffle places B before A) and never on 5005 (the seed that keeps A first), matching the catalog's offline-simulated expectation exactly and never varying.

Ground-truth flaky fixture (test_flaky_probability, OS-entropy-seeded, ~40% intrinsic failure rate) was correctly classified by probe2 on every one of the 3 probe2 runs: flagged=True with a mixed pass/fail outcome vector across the 5 identical-order repeats, proving probe2's independent-process-repeat harness is not caching/memoizing a single result.

The real (non-planted) 135-test corpus was NEVER flagged by either probe across all 9 total probe invocations (6x probe1 + 3x probe2) in this review: every order-dependent candidate probe1 ever produced was one of the two planted fixtures, and every flaky test probe2 ever produced was the one planted flaky fixture. This directly confirms the artifact's headline claim 'real 135-test corpus: 0 order-dependent, 0 flaky this pass' is robust, not a single-run fluke.

Cross-reference/set-difference logic is doing real work, not decoration: on one of my 6 probe1 re-runs (matching the original artifact's own recorded raw output almost exactly), the planted flaky fixture ALSO showed baseline-pass-then-shuffle-fail behavior purely by chance and would have inflated the naive order-dependent count to 2 if probe1 were trusted alone; probe2's independent flaky classification of that same fixture is what correctly demotes it to flake-explained rather than genuine order-dependence. This is direct empirical proof of exactly the confound the catalog's evidence_requirement warns about, and proof the census's two-probe design (not just probe1) is necessary and sufficient to resolve it.

The genuine_order_dependent_count of 1 (test_b_requires_writer_flag) was the ONE quantity that stayed perfectly invariant across every single re-run regardless of the flaky fixture's random draw -- this is the correct invariant for the headline finding and it held.

The 138-test collectible scope is legitimate, not artificially narrowed to dodge a bad result: re-running `pytest --collect-only` over command-center/ WITHOUT the two --ignore flags reproduces exactly the 3 collection errors collectible_scope.py documents (scratch_pkg_good, b5-toolchain mcp-manager, wt-salvage-probe codex_profiles), each a genuine ModuleNotFoundError/FileNotFoundError unrelated to order or flakiness, confirming the exclusions are a real scoping decision, not a cover for a different result.
